chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: A man came to my brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) and said to him: May I be your ransom, I intend to go out, so pray for me. He said: When will you go out? He said: On Monday. He said to him: Why do you go out on Monday? He said: I seek blessings in it because the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was born on Monday. He said: They lied. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was born on Friday. And no day is greater in ill-omen than Monday, the day on which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) died and the revelation of heaven ceased on it, and we were wronged in it regarding our right. Shall I not guide you to an easy day on which God softened iron for David (peace be upon him)? The man said: Yes, may I be your ransom. He said: Go out on Tuesday.

key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) advise against traveling on Monday?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) corrects the common belief that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was born on Monday, asserting instead that Friday holds greater significance as the day of his death and the cessation of revelation, which also marks the time when the Ahl al-Bayt were deprived of their due right. The Imam contrasts the perceived auspiciousness of Monday with the ease of Tuesday, referencing the divine softening of iron for Prophet David (AS) on that day, thereby linking temporal blessings to specific historical and spiritual events in Shia tradition.
